# Turned Away, and Told Why

Version 3.2.0 is about what happens when bergfex refuses a request. You now learn that it happened and what to do about it, and the integration asks bergfex for far fewer pages to begin with.

## When bergfex refuses a request

- **A refusal now says what refused.** _[#57]_ bergfex sits behind Cloudflare, and a block page carries its reason in the response and a ray ID in the headers. Until now both were thrown away, so the log could only say `403, message='Forbidden'`. The status, the ray ID and the start of the block page are now kept.
- **Both URLs are reported.** bergfex redirects German resorts from `www.bergfex.at` to `www.bergfex.de`, so the URL in the error used to be the end of the redirect, not the address the integration asked for. Both now appear side by side whenever they differ.
- **A repair notice replaces endless retrying.** After five refusals in a row, Home Assistant shows a notice that names the host, the status and the ray ID, and suggests a way out. You get one notice per host, however many resorts sit behind it. It clears itself as soon as a request gets through. A notice left over from before a restart is dropped once nothing still backs it up.
- **The diagnostics download carries the evidence.** An entry that is refused never finishes setting up, so its diagnostics used to be empty, and that is exactly the entry a bug report is about. The refusal details are now included.
- **The setup dialog no longer blames your internet connection.** Adding a resort or changing an entry's language checks the page first. Every failure used to show *"Please check your internet connection"*, even when the connection was fine and bergfex had refused it. A refusal now says so. An empty resort list caused by a refused country overview says so too.
- **A missing page is not a refusal.** Only 403, 429 and 451 count. A 404 or a bad moment at bergfex does not raise the notice.

## German resorts and `www.bergfex.de`

Since mid-October, `www.bergfex.de` refuses clients that are not a web browser on some connections. That includes Home Assistant, whatever user agent it sends, while browsers on the same network open the site normally. Only German resorts are affected. In German, the integration asks `www.bergfex.at`, and bergfex sends German resorts on to `www.bergfex.de` from there. Every other language uses a bergfex domain that serves those resorts itself.

If your German resorts fail with 403, open the entry, choose **Reconfigure** and pick another language. English keeps the readings easy to read. Entities, device and history stay as they are. Only the text taken from the page, such as snow and slope condition, arrives in the new language.

## Fewer requests

- **Region pages are shared.** The region snow report and the cross-country overview list every area at once, but each entry fetched its own copy. Entries in the same region now share one copy for ten minutes.
- **Entries polling at the same time wait for each other.** All entries poll together, so several used to ask for the same page before the first answer arrived. A page that is already being fetched is now awaited instead of requested again.
- **Forecast pages are kept for three hours instead of ten minutes.** bergfex updates the snow-forecast images only a few times a day. This alone was about half of all requests.

On an installation with seventeen entries, these changes take a poll from about seventy requests to about thirty.

## Fixes

- **French installations keep their "last updated" time.** About one page in three shortens "Aujourd'hui" to "Auj.", and those polls produced no timestamp. Both spellings are now read.

## Upgrading

Nothing to change after updating. If you were on a 3.2.0 beta, this is the same code as `beta.5`.
